newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish higher on U.S. market boost.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish higher on U.S. market boost.

text.p: French shares finished higher on Thursday, lifted in the afternoon by strength in U.S. stock and debt markets after opening lower and spending most of the session stuck nearly unchanged.
Dealers said the market would be sharply focussed on December's U.S. non-farm payrolls report due at 1330 GMT on Friday. Analysts in a Reuter poll expect 192,000 jobs were created last month.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed 17.46 points or 0.75 higher percent at 2,349.08 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 8.5 points at 1606 GMT.
Volume was a hefty 8.1 billion francs.
U.S. markets climbed on news that December producer prices rose 0.1 percent excluding food and energy. For 1996, overall producer prices rose 2.8 percent, the smallest gain since 1993.
The tame numbers sent most European stock markets higher by calming inflation fears and reassuring investors that a near-term tightening of U.S. monetary policy was unlikely.
Paribas closed up 4.02 percent at 345.20 francs after announcing that its Credit du Nord unit would be sold to Societe Generale.
Societe Generale, the second most heavily traded share in Paris on Thursday, ended 2.22 percent higher at 552 francs.
Traders said the deal keeps merger interest alive in the French financial sector. Rumours were circulating recently over an acquisition in the sector although the names were vague.
Saint Gobain closed 4.85 percent higher at 779 francs after buy recommendations from at least two French brokers as interest in cyclical stocks rose.
Broker Leven said in a note to clients St that Gobain is undervalued by as much as 30 percent in relation to the Paris Bourse's price/earnings ratio.
Generale des Eaux closed up 3.06 percent at 708 francs as the share continued to rise after successfully cutting its debt and reaffirming its profit forecast for 1996.
Valeo ended up 0.96 percent at 348.30 francs after posting 1996 sales up 14.4 percent, in line with expectations.
Alcatel Alsthom closed up 0.82 percent at 431 francs as investors bet on a potential benefit from buying Thomson-CSF, contrary to earlier fears such a purchase would be a burden.
